we have designed two broadband InP HBT PAs that demonstrate 80-70 GHz large-signal bandwidth and 200–248 mW peak output power between 180-265 GHz.
we have demonstrated 100-m W power to 255 GHz and 70-GHZ (16-cell) and 80- GHZ (8-cell) bandwidth covering most WR04 band.

we have demonstrated two InP HBT broadband power amplifier chips operating at 250-nm, covering the WR-4 waveguide frequency band, that have 70-GHz and 80-GH z bandwidths and deliver 100-mW and 50-m W power to 255- and 263-GHz, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a high-power, high-gain, broadband InP HBT MMIC amplifier for use as a transmitter driver in the 180- to 260-GHz frequency band for use in the WR04 waveguides.
the design and fabrication of high-performance power amplifiers operating at millimeter-wave and sub-THz frequencies.
developing high-performance, low-cost, and compact InP HBT amplifiers that operate in the 180–265-GHz band.

The main takeaway from our work is that
high power and high gain can be obtained in the 180–265-GHz band using InP HBT technology, and that the power and gain bandwidth can be increased by increasing the number of PA cells in the design.
the InP HBT is a very attractive technology for broadband high-power amplifiers at millimeter-wave frequencies.
InP HBTs can be used as the technology of choice to realize high-gain, high-power amplifiers in the millimeter-wave range.
